function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or instruction that gives someone the power or right to act on behalf of another person or entity. It can take many forms depending on the context:

| Context | What a mandate typically means |
|---------|--------------------------------|
| **Legal/Contractual** | A written or verbal agreement that authorizes one party (the agent) to perform certain actions for another (the principal). For example, a power‑of‑attorney document allows a lawyer to sign contracts on your behalf. |
| **Financial** | An order or instruction given to a broker or bank to execute trades, manage investments, or handle payments. In this sense, a mandate often refers to a set of rules or preferences that govern how a portfolio is managed. |
| **Political** | A directive from a governing body or electorate that empowers a leader or institution to pursue a particular policy agenda. For instance, a government may have a “mandate” to reduce carbon emissions. |
| **Business** | A contract or assignment that delegates responsibility for a project or task to a vendor or contractor. |

In short, a mandate is a formal delegation of authority that specifies what actions can be taken, by whom, and under what conditions.
